results.linear_center_quadratic_projection: For a linear center and e=2, exact division gives D=alpha U+D0(V), and the actual triple-ring equality yields O=L[theta,wtilde] with y=U0-R wtilde/B1. After completing theta's square over the exact field L, the odd-part generation argument forces wtilde=P(theta)+b1 x, with b1 a nonzero element of L. It follows that C=L[y,theta]=L[x^2,x^3+c1x] is a proper plane ring of defect dimension one, with conductor exactly(x^2+c1)O=RO. It is geometrically a node when c1 is nonzero and a cusp when c1 is zero.
